FR.1: FR1. The system shall maintain one PIR collection in memory and shall start each session with an empty collection. It shall not automatically load a previous file.
FR.2: FR2. The system shall assign a newly created PIR the next positive integer above the highest PIR ID successfully allocated or loaded in the current session, starting at 1. Deletion shall not lower this allocation counter. Loading shall restore saved IDs rather than allocate new ones, and shall raise the counter if a loaded ID is higher. Failed, declined or cancelled operations shall not advance the counter.
FR.3: FR3. Every PIR shall have exactly one type: PLAIN_TEXT, TASK, EVENT or CONTACT. IDs shall be unique within the current collection.
FR.4: FR4. The system shall allow creation of a PLAIN_TEXT PIR with note text satisfying Section 5.3.
FR.5: FR5. The system shall allow creation of a TASK PIR with a description and deadline satisfying Section 5.3.
FR.6: FR6. The system shall allow creation of an EVENT PIR with a description, starting time and alarm time satisfying Section 5.3. The alarm shall be earlier than or equal to the starting time.
FR.7: FR7. The system shall allow creation of a CONTACT PIR with a name, address and mobile number satisfying Section 5.3. Mobile numbers shall be stored as text so that leading zeroes are preserved.
FR.8: FR8. If a required field is missing or invalid, the system shall reject the complete creation request, report the reason and leave records and ID allocation unchanged. The user may submit a corrected command.
FR.9: FR9. The system shall allow modification of one business field of a PIR selected by ID. The complete resulting record shall satisfy the creation rules, including the Event alarm/start relationship. ID and type shall not be editable.
FR.10: FR10. If the ID is invalid or absent, the field is not editable for that record type, or the new value is invalid, the system shall report an error and leave all records unchanged.
FR.11: FR11. The system shall return every current PIR satisfying a directly supplied search expression or a previously defined criterion selected by criterion ID. Searching shall not change records.
FR.12: FR12. The system shall support type = X, where X is PLAIN_TEXT, TASK, EVENT or CONTACT. This condition shall be true exactly when the PIR has type X.
FR.13: FR13. The system shall support field ~ "substring" for text, description, name, address and mobile fields as defined in Section 5.3. It shall use case-sensitive, consecutive substring matching. The quoted substring shall be non-empty and shall be preserved without trimming; whitespace and underscores are valid search characters. The ~ symbol shall not invoke regular expressions or wildcards.
FR.14: FR14. The system shall support field < T, field > T and field = T for deadline, start and alarm. T shall be a quoted date-time satisfying Section 5.3. Comparisons shall use the complete date and time at minute precision.
FR.15: FR15. The system shall support ! for negation, && for conjunction, || for disjunction and parentheses for grouping. Atomic comparisons shall form Boolean operands; logical precedence shall be !, then &&, then ||. Parentheses shall override logical precedence. NOT is true when its operand is false; AND requires both operands to be true; OR requires at least one operand to be true. Written keywords AND, OR, NOT and CONTAINS shall not be alternative operators.
FR.16: FR16. An atomic field condition shall be false for a PIR lacking that field. Logical combinations shall use that Boolean result. An unrecognised field name shall instead be an error under FR17.
FR.17: FR17. The system shall reject invalid expression syntax, unknown fields, incompatible field/operator combinations, invalid time literals and unknown criterion IDs with an error, without returning a result set or changing records.
FR.18: FR18. The system shall display matching PIRs in ascending numerical PIR ID order, including each ID, type and all business fields. When no PIR matches, it shall explicitly report zero matches. A count for non-empty results is not required.
FR.19: FR19. Given an existing PIR ID, the system shall display its ID, type and all business fields. An invalid or absent ID shall produce an error.
FR.20: FR20. The system shall display the ID, type and all business fields of every PIR in ascending numerical ID order when display-all is requested. It shall report an empty collection explicitly.
FR.21: FR21. Before deleting a PIR selected by ID, the system shall display its details and request confirmation. Confirmation shall delete only that PIR; refusal shall leave the collection unchanged. An invalid or absent ID shall produce an error without changing records.
FR.22: FR22. The system shall save the entire collection, including an empty collection, to a user-selected path ending in .pim. Saved records shall be ordered by ascending ID and include ID, type and every business field. Search criteria shall not be included.
FR.23: FR23. If saving fails because the destination is invalid or cannot be written, the system shall report an error and preserve the in-memory collection, ID counter and any unsaved-changes status. Success shall be reported only after writing completes successfully.
FR.24: FR24. The system shall load a supported .pim file and, after successful complete validation and resolution of unsaved changes, replace the current collection with exactly its saved records. Original IDs shall be restored. Loading shall not merge collections or assign replacement IDs. A valid empty file collection shall replace the current collection with an empty one.
FR.25: FR25. The system shall reject a missing, unreadable or invalid file. Validation shall check supported types, required fields, field rules, positive integer IDs and unique IDs within the file before any replacement. On failure the collection and ID allocation shall remain unchanged. Existing unsaved changes shall remain unless the user successfully saved them before the failed load.
FR.26: FR26. Saving and loading shall preserve the number of records, all IDs, types and business field values, including Unicode text and mobile-number leading zeroes. Record output shall follow ascending ID order. Distinct IDs may have identical business contents; loading shall neither remove such records nor prompt for duplicate-content confirmation.
FR.27: FR27. The system shall expose creation, modification, criterion definition, search, display, deletion, saving and loading through text commands and arguments entered in the terminal. Operations shall not require numbered menu navigation.
FR.28: FR28. Unknown commands and invalid arguments shall produce an error and return control to the command prompt. Invalid mutating commands shall leave records unchanged. There is no reserved :cancel field-entry mechanism.
FR.29: FR29. The system shall provide an exit command. Exit shall be subject to the unsaved-changes rules in FR35–FR36.
FR.30: FR30. The system shall allow the user to define a valid search expression and assign it a unique session identifier C1, C2 and so on. It shall display the assigned identifier and expression and provide a way to list defined criteria. Invalid expressions shall not create criteria. Defined criteria shall remain unchanged; a changed expression shall be defined as a new criterion.
FR.31: FR31. Defined criteria shall remain available throughout the session, including after record changes and successful loads, and shall evaluate the current collection when used. They shall not be saved in .pim files and shall be cleared when the session ends.
FR.32: FR32. Before committing a valid creation request, the system shall check for an existing PIR of the same type with identical values in every business field after input normalization. IDs shall be excluded and text comparison shall be case-sensitive. If a duplicate exists, the system shall warn and request confirmation. Confirmation shall add a separate PIR with a new ID; refusal shall add nothing. Duplicate-content confirmation shall apply to creation only; editing or loading may produce identical contents under different IDs without this prompt.
FR.33: FR33. Before saving over an existing file, the system shall request overwrite confirmation. Refusal shall preserve that file and the in-memory collection and shall not count as a successful save.
FR.34: FR34. The system shall mark the collection as having unsaved changes after successful creation, deletion or an edit that changes a value. Read-only, invalid, refused and no-change operations shall not introduce changes. Startup, successful save and successful load shall establish a state without unsaved changes.
FR.35: FR35. Before exit or load when unsaved changes exist, the system shall offer save and continue, discard and continue, or cancel. Cancellation shall preserve the collection and keep the current session active. Discard during loading shall not remove the old collection until the replacement file has passed complete validation.
FR.36: FR36. If save and continue is selected, the system shall continue with exit or load only after saving succeeds. A failed save or declined overwrite shall stop the pending action and retain the records and any unsaved changes. The user may retry saving or explicitly choose to discard. If saving succeeds but a subsequent load fails, the saved current collection shall remain available with no unsaved changes.

UR.1: UR1. The user shall be able to manage plain-text, task, event and contact PIRs in one collection.
UR.2: UR2. The user shall be able to create a plain-text PIR containing a note.
UR.3: UR3. The user shall be able to create a task PIR containing a description and deadline.
UR.4: UR4. The user shall be able to create an event PIR containing a description, starting time and alarm time.
UR.5: UR5. The user shall be able to create a contact PIR containing a name, address and mobile number.
UR.6: UR6. The user shall be able to modify the business fields of an existing PIR.
UR.7: UR7. The user shall be able to search by type, text and time, including criteria combined with &&, || and !.
UR.8: UR8. The user shall be able to display detailed information about one PIR or all PIRs.
UR.9: UR9. The user shall be able to delete a specified PIR.
UR.10: UR10. The user shall be able to save the current PIR collection to a .pim file.
UR.11: UR11. The user shall be able to load a saved PIR collection and continue working with it.

NFR.1: NFR1. Every error shall begin with ERROR and include a short reason identifying the affected input or operation. Where relevant, feedback shall state the expected format or allowed values.
NFR.2: NFR2. Invalid commands, fields, criteria and expected file-operation errors shall not terminate the program through an unhandled exception. Validation and load failures shall preserve state as specified in FR8, FR10, FR17 and FR25.
NFR.3: NFR3. All code belonging to the model shall reside in model and shall be callable independently of terminal input and output. This includes any persistence code classified as model behaviour. Command parsing, prompting and output formatting shall remain separately identifiable.
NFR.4: NFR4. The system shall run on Windows with the Python version identified in the developer manual, without third-party runtime Python packages.
NFR.5: NFR5. All specified record, search and file operations shall work without a network connection.
